headline: Week eight: deload nudges over target, run reintro clean
narrative: Deload week, and the number landed on the wrong side of the line — a small overshoot on a target built to be undershot, with the surplus mostly down to one big session. Travel to York split the week in two: Monday's club run and Thursday's Higher Moor trail run bookended largely social walking days away from home, then Sunday closed the gap with an incline treadmill session on a borrowed gym pass — mostly walking at steep grade with the odd stride — that alone supplied most of the week's climbing. Time on feet did land under the ask, so the legs still got the easier week even if the vert line didn't quite behave.

The week's real job was the run reintroduction check, and that passed clean: Monday's club run, Saturday's parkrun, and the running portion of Sunday's treadmill work all went through without a word about the calf — the first week back with three genuine running sessions since rehab began, and it held. That clears the way into next week's move to Build, which asks for run reintro on flat-to-gentle terrain if cleared, while still hiking the vert. The block absorbs cleanly; onward into Build.
